title: Reaching Somebody
label: ch:ml-message
canDo: I can name the telephone, a letter, the post, e-mail and the internet, and say an address aloud as far as the stop.

payoff.summary: From cold: five ways of reaching somebody, and the letter the chapter had to buy first.
payoff.note: FIVE SPANISH POINTS BEHIND ONE MALAYALAM POINT -- A1-NE09-01..03, NE09-06 and NE11-01 -- which made LEX-38 the largest single payoff left in the file. THE NOTE'S 'Nothing' HELD, and the check that confirmed it is the one that has caught me before: kattu (a letter) LOOKS taught, because grepping for it matches inside akattu ('inside', ML-C95). Word-bounded against the Malayalam block it returns ZERO. Count the token, not the substring -- and the lesson turns that near-miss into teaching, showing the learner the overlap so it cannot mislead them, using ML-C95's own advice to read the ends and not the fronts. FOUR OF THE FIVE WORDS COST NO SCRIPT DEBT. kattu, thapaal and imeyil use only glyphs already shown and directly owned; inrarneRRu deepens the already-open chillu-r (11/11 to 12/12) and opens nothing new. shown stays 68 and the owned overlap stays 59. THE TELEPHONE IS TAUGHT BY EAR, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY. phooN needs the chillu NN, which ML-S131 teaches at sequence 144 but data/scripts/malayalam.json omits, so writing it trips uncovered-glyphs and integration.test.ts turns that queue into a hard failure. HL-C398 records why a curriculum chapter must NOT simply add the entry: every listed chillu is pinned to a SOURCED stroke-order animation, the inventory says outright that 'a citation cannot be guessed', and script inventories are a different owner's surface by design (HL24). Fabricating the citation or crossing that boundary were both refused. The word is given in romanization with the lesson telling the learner plainly that its written shape comes when its letter does -- chapter 88's precedent for eighty, and ML-C07-numbers-6-10's before that. A DRAFT WAS THROWN AWAY TO GET THERE. The first version bought a new letter, ML-S148-letter-pha, so that phooN could be printed: pha is the breath-partner of pa and appears in NO headword in the corpus. Validate then failed on the chillu, not on pha -- and once the word could not be printed, buying a letter to write it was incoherent, so the script lesson was deleted rather than kept for appearance. The chapter is five lessons, not six. THE E-MAIL LESSON IS WHERE CHAPTER 108 PAYS OFF: saying an address aloud needs the FULL STOP, taught with the other marks, and the lesson says honestly that the mark before the domain still has no Malayalam name here -- the same call the punctuation chapter made about the marks' names.
